thread:
maria: FYI — three customers reported a flood of "error-rate > 5%" alerts around 07:14 UTC. Dashboards show many zero/empty points but alerts still triggered.

Aisha: thanks @maria. sample cust ids and alert link?

maria: cust: cust_78a, cust_90b, cust_12c
alert: https://console.redwood.example.com/alerts/abc123
window: 07:00-07:20 UTC

jonathan: I see a rollout at 07:05 that changed rollup.align_to from "auto" to "minute" for sparse namespaces. deploy log:

```
deploy infra/rollups
commit 4f2d9a
changed: rollup.policy.align_to: auto -> minute
applied: metrics.namespace=customer_events (sparse=true)
```

leo: aligning to minute can create empty minute buckets for sparse counters, which makes relative rates spike on single events.

maria: repro on staging:
1) query rollup(namespace="customer_events", metric="error_rate", rollup=60s, align_to=minute)
2) 07:00-07:20
3) got zeros and one 0.12 at 07:04 -> relative threshold crosses because denominator tiny

sample:
```
[07:00] 0.0
[07:01] 0.0
[07:04] 0.12
[07:05] 0.0
```

alerts-bot: "error-rate>5%" fired 89x between 07:14-07:16 for cust_78a, cust_90b, cust_12c

deploy-bot: rollback commit 4f2d9a at 07:22 (rollback-id d1b7c)

jonathan: rollback stopped the noise. root cause: minute alignment for sparse series created tiny denominators. fixes:
- detect sparse streams and preserve native timestamps (PR: https://git.internal/redwood/rollups/pulls/456)
- unit test for relative-alerts on sparse rollups
- add alert guard: ignore windows with <N samples when metric marked sparse

maria: customer comms sent (ETA ~2h for full fix). they appreciated prompt rollback note :thumbsup:

leo: incident triaged, watching for 2h then close.

maria: will draft postmortem and close thread.
